description: SPI idle-state pulls at the module
notes: SIX, not three - BOTH SIDES of the 74AHCT125. Cable side: CS to +5V, SCLK and MOSI to ground, so the buffer's inputs do not float and crowbar when the instrument is absent. DAC side: same, because with OE disabled the buffer outputs are Hi-Z and it is then the DAC's SCLK/DIN/SYNC that float - which is the state these were bought for and the three cable-side pulls do not reach. Module-alive-instrument-off is the normal state, not a fault; a stray CS edge latches garbage into the pitch DAC. CABLE-SIDE CS PULLS TO 3V3, NOT +5V: pulled to 5V it drives 430uA continuously through the unpowered ESP32's input clamp in the design's NORMAL resting state, and the node sits at ~0.7V so 'CS idle high' is not even achieved. DAC-SIDE CS PULLS TO AVDD (the LM317's 5.21V), not bus +5V - a pull-up belongs on its consumer's rail, and on the bus rail a reversed ribbon reaches the DAC's SYNC pin and turns a $0.30 buffer failure into a DAC failure

description: Series termination on SCLK, MOSI and CS at the driving end
notes: THREE. 100R, not 220R - revised 2026-09-21. 2m of Cat5 is a 100-ohm TRANSMISSION LINE (20ns round trip against 2-5ns edges), not an RC corner, and three reviewers agreed the old RC derivation was the wrong model. At 220R the far end's first step is 1.83-1.86V against the 74AHCT125's 2.0V VIH, dwelling ~20ns per edge in the forbidden band on a part with no hysteresis. 100R gives a clean 2.75V single step and 33mA of fault current; 68R is electrically ideal but draws 48mA against a 40mA pad spec. carrier.md used to draw these as R-SCLK-SER / R-MOSI-SER / R-CS-SER, which were in no BOM

description: ESD protection on the umbilical's SPI lines
notes: SCLK, MOSI, CS (+ one spare channel) to PWR_GND. REPLACES U-TVS-UMB, which named SP3012-06UTG: that part is obsolete AND uDFN-14, not the SOT-23-6 the row claimed - leadless fine pitch, banned by the ADR 0013 package policy. It was un-orderable as written | 2026-09-21, SECOND PART CHECKED AND REJECTED FOR THE SAME REASON: onsemi ESD7104 is a genuine 4-channel 5V array (V_RWM 5.0V, V_BR 5.5V, V_C 10V at I_PP 1A 8/20us) and looks like a clean answer - but it ships ONLY in UDFN10 (case 517BB) and WDFNW10 (case 515AH, 2.5 x 1.0mm, 0.5mm pitch). Leadless fine pitch, banned by the same ADR 0013 policy. DO NOT RE-PROPOSE IT. Recorded here rather than only in the manifest because this row is where the next reader looks. ALSO: the 0.98W sustained-fault figure this row's protection budget assumes has never had a source, and there is now a reason to doubt the QUESTION. The ESD7104 datasheet specifies the part purely by PULSE (8/20us, IEC 61000-4-2) and states no steady-state power dissipation at all - which suggests a sustained-fault rating may be outside what this whole class of array is specified for, whichever part is chosen. That is an INFERENCE FROM A DIFFERENT PART and must be confirmed against the SP0504BAHT itself, which is still BLOCKED. If it holds, the right fix is a series resistor or a resettable element, not a bigger array | 2026-09-21 PACKAGE REFUTED AND THE POWER FIGURE DELETED. SP050xBA datasheet banked at datasheets/discrete-and-power/SP0504BAHT.pdf (Littelfuse databook extract pp.220-227, via farnell.com; littelfuse.com is 403 at the proxy). *** SP0504BAHTG IS SOT-23-5, NOT SOT-23-6. *** p.1 ordering table: SP0504BAHTG | 4 CH | SOT23-5, and SP0505BAHTG | 5 CH | SOT23-6. Confirmed against the package outline drawings pp.6-7. This row asserted SOT-23-6, which is exactly the unchecked-package error it exists to replace U-TVS-UMB for. FIX: either this row becomes SOT-23-5, or it moves to SP0505BAHTG which genuinely is SOT-23-6 and brings a fifth channel. Package changed to SOT-23-5 here; the 0.95mm pitch was right, so the ADR 0013 package-policy reasoning survives. *** THE 0.98 W FIGURE IS DELETED, NOT CORRECTED. *** Abs Max p.2 gives package power dissipation 0.225 W for SOT23-3/-5/-6/SOT143, corroborated p.7 'PD@70degC .225W' - the review's 0.98W was optimistic by 4.4x. But the more important finding is that THERE IS NO PEAK PULSE POWER SPEC AT ALL: no I_PP, no 8/20us or 10/1000us waveform, no surge curve, no theta-JA anywhere in the 8 pages. The part is ESD-rated only (IEC 61000-4-2, 20kV contact / 30kV air), so a surge-energy claim cannot be sourced from it. 30 pF per channel is high for a modern array (USB1.1-era part) - against 2m of Cat5 and R-SPI-SER this is ~29ns of edge on a 250ns half-period at 2MHz, acceptable, but it is the first time TVS capacitance has entered the umbilical edge budget. ALL FOUR CHANNELS SHARE ONE COMMON PIN (pin 2), so a single array cannot straddle PWR_GND and DIG_GND - which supports keeping U-TVS-SPI and U-TVS-CHAIN as two packages. The array is effectively UNI-DIRECTIONAL: the -0.8V negative clamp is a forward diode drop, not an avalanche knee. Fine for 0-3.3V SPI; MUST NOT be reused on a bipolar CV node | *** AND IT REFUTES THE ESD7104 INFERENCE RECORDED JUST ABOVE, WHICH I FIRST WROTE UP AS CONFIRMING IT. *** That observation was correctly flagged as 'an inference from a DIFFERENT part [that] must be confirmed against the SP0504BAHT itself'. Confirmed against the part, IT DOES NOT HOLD - the two documents are mirror images. The ESD7104 specifies PULSE ONLY (8/20us, IEC 61000-4-2) and states no steady-state dissipation. The SP0504BAHT is the other way round: it DOES specify steady-state package power dissipation, 0.225 W for SOT23-5, in Absolute Maximum Ratings p.2, corroborated by 'PD@70degC .225W' in the p.7 package table - and it specifies NO PULSE RATING AT ALL. No I_PP, no peak pulse power, no 8/20us or 10/1000us waveform, no surge or pulse-derating curve, and no thetaJA for any package. The only occurrence of 'pulse' in 8 pages is a V-I graph's measurement condition. SO A SUSTAINED-FAULT RATING IS NOT OUTSIDE WHAT THIS PART IS SPECIFIED FOR - it is 0.225 W, a published hard ceiling, and that makes the case STRONGER not vaguer: the prior review's 0.98 W is refuted by a real sourced number 4.4x lower, so the right fix remains a series resistor or a resettable element rather than a bigger array. What IS genuinely missing here is the pulse side, which is what an ESD array would normally be specified by.
